FIELD_036.context: A crane serves two rebar crews; both need finished cages lifted in the first half of the shift.
FIELD_036.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will propose my own allocation of lifts and, together with the foremen, check whether the sequence is feasible.
options.B: I will name the priority based on the readiness of the cages and establish the order of lifts in advance.
options.C: I will briefly coordinate time slots with the supervisors and the crane operator.
options.D: I will propose a justified sequence and agree the order of lifts with the participants.

FIELD_037.context: After the cage was assembled, it was found that the starter bars for a column are close to the design axis but outside the tolerance.
FIELD_037.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will recheck the as-built survey and the tolerances to establish the size and cause of the offset.
options.B: I will not release the joint for concreting until a formal technical solution is issued.
options.C: I will check the measurements, record the deviation and obtain a confirmed decision before the pour.
options.D: I will compare the actual position of the starter bars with the design and file a request for a technical solution.

FIELD_038.context: During a prolonged concrete pour, a pause is approaching the maximum permissible interval.
FIELD_038.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will firmly prevent pumping from resuming until the responsible concrete technologist makes a decision.
options.B: I will state the time limit, present the data to the concrete technologist and organise continuation in line with the approved decision.
options.C: I will assess the length of the pause from the supply log and personally set out the conditions for continuing to the person in charge.
options.D: I will check the actual time, the mix properties and the placement chart, then assess an acceptable option.

FIELD_039.context: On site two batches of rebar of the same diameter lie side by side, but the marking of one is partly lost.
FIELD_039.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the documents and, together with the warehouse, mark the confirmed bundles before issue.
options.B: I will ask the warehouse and the rebar workers to restore the batch information and compare it with the markings.
options.C: I will check the documents and markings of the remaining bundles to restore traceability.
options.D: I will gather the storekeeper and the foreman to identify the batches separately.

FIELD_040.context: Before lifting an assembled formwork panel, the sling log shows an overdue inspection.
FIELD_040.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will personally arrange for the slings to be replaced and record confirmation of readiness before lifting the panel.
options.B: I will record the overdue sling inspection in the log and file a request for a serviceable set.
options.C: I will not allow lifting with this set and will demand a serviceable, inspected sling.
options.D: I will check the log against the markings and arrange a replacement before lifting resumes.

FIELD_041.context: After the pour the pump must be washed out, but the area at the agreed washout point is temporarily occupied.
FIELD_041.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check an alternative against the waste management scheme and formalise the change of washout point.
options.B: I will contact the site environmental officer and the operator to free up or agree another location.
options.C: I will keep the requirement for the washout location and agree an available option with those responsible.
options.D: I will agree another approved washout location with the operator and update the close-out procedure.

FIELD_042.context: After finishing the pour section a few cubic metres of mix are left over; the neighbouring crew is preparing another structure.
FIELD_042.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will contact the neighbouring supervisor and the laboratory to check together whether it can be used.
options.B: I will take responsibility for agreeing the time limits and quality requirements for the mix, then agree on acceptable use with the neighbouring crew.
options.C: I will suggest discussing the surplus with the neighbouring crew and take responsibility for asking whether it can be used.
options.D: I will make clear that the mix can be used only with confirmed suitability and a permit for a specific area.

FIELD_043.context: After storage, surface deposits were found on some rebar; the degree of corrosion is difficult to assess visually.
FIELD_043.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the condition with the inspector and formalise a decision on suitability before issue.
options.B: I will compare the surface deposits with the inspection criteria and document the specialist's decision on the batch.
options.C: I will compare the condition with the design and incoming inspection requirements and arrange an objective assessment.
options.D: I will separate the disputed batch and arrange its inspection before it is sent to the section.

FIELD_044.context: After the slab pour, another crew wants to store heavy formwork on the recently concreted slab.
FIELD_044.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will prepare information on strength and loads and personally propose that the structural engineer check the storage scheme.
options.B: I will check the age and confirmed strength of the concrete, the permissible load and the storage scheme.
options.C: I will clearly prohibit placement until the bearing capacity is confirmed and propose an alternative area.
options.D: I will present the calculated limits and agree another storage location with the crew.

FIELD_045.context: During the formwork inspection a local leak of cement laitance was noticed at one joint.
FIELD_045.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will assess the location and extent of the leak, then check the prescribed sealing method.
options.B: I will gather the formwork supervisor and the technologist to choose an acceptable joint repair.
options.C: I will record the defect and, together with the supervisor, agree the fix before supply continues.
options.D: I will collect the observations of the operator and the carpenters to determine the source of the leak together.

FIELD_046.context: The shift assignment schedules formwork stripping for the morning, but there is no confirmation of the required strength yet.
FIELD_046.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will not allow stripping until the required strength is confirmed and a permit is issued.
options.B: I will check the results and, together with the responsible person, formalise a decision on the acceptable date.
options.C: I will set the deadline for receiving the strength results myself and establish the procedure for issuing the stripping permit.
options.D: I will note the missing confirmation in the shift assignment and postpone stripping until a permit is issued.

FIELD_047.context: The embedded part installers ask to combine two small inspections into one so as not to hold up the crew.
FIELD_047.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the inspection requirements and, together with the participants, confirm acceptable inspection time slots.
options.B: I will agree joint preparation for the inspections with the installers while keeping each control point recorded separately.
options.C: I will keep the mandatory inspection stages in the schedule and notify the responsible inspector.
options.D: I will discuss with the installers and the inspector whether the sequence can be safely rearranged.

FIELD_048.context: Two rebar crews are arguing about whose turn it is to work in the limited work area in the stairwell.
FIELD_048.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will propose my own division of the stairwell work area and, together with the foremen, clarify the order of operations.
options.B: I will name the access order based on the readiness of the previous operations and take responsibility for the sequence.
options.C: I will bring the foremen together and agree the time, access and work area handover points.
options.D: I will determine a justified order and confirm the work time slots together with the foremen.

FIELD_049.context: Before applying the finishing putty, the moisture of the base on one wall is higher than the neighbouring readings.
FIELD_049.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will recheck the measurement points and conditions and compare them with the requirements of the mix and the base.
options.B: I will postpone finishing this wall until its readiness is confirmed according to the method statement.
options.C: I will repeat the measurements, record the result and schedule finishing once the permissible value is reached.
options.D: I will compare the moisture readings with the application conditions and record the decision on the wall's readiness.

FIELD_050.context: During a facade anchor test, one value is close to the set limit, while the others are higher.
FIELD_050.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will say directly that the borderline result requires a decision by the quality control service before continuing on this area.
options.B: I will present the test report and propose a control test under an agreed programme.
options.C: I will check the conditions of the borderline test and propose to the responsible person myself a way to confirm the result.
options.D: I will study the test report, the sampling scheme and the condition of the base before drawing a conclusion on the batch.

FIELD_051.context: Ceiling installers found that an air duct passes through the designated hanger fixing point.
FIELD_051.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the clash against the drawings and, together with the adjacent trades, formalise an acceptable change.
options.B: I will compare the fixing conflict with the duct route and prepare a joint detail option with the adjacent trades.
options.C: I will check the system drawings and the permissible fixing zones to determine the source of the conflict.
options.D: I will gather the ventilation crew, the ceiling installers and the designer at the joint to agree a solution.

FIELD_052.context: Paint of the right shade has arrived at the warehouse, but for some of the buckets the shelf life requires an additional check.
FIELD_052.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will set the procedure for checking shelf lives myself and record the status of each part of the paint batch.
options.B: I will set aside the buckets with unconfirmed shelf life and arrange a check during incoming inspection.
options.C: I will block issue of the disputed batch until a formal decision is made on its suitability.
options.D: I will split the batch, check the documents and authorise use only of the verified buckets.

FIELD_053.context: The cladding sample has been approved, but the new crew has not yet seen it before starting work.
FIELD_053.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will include viewing the sample and the control parameters in the shift assignment.
options.B: I will show the crew the sample on site and we will discuss what acceptable workmanship looks like.
options.C: I will check the work chart against the sample, then record a control point together with the crew.
options.D: I will arrange for the sample to be shown to the new crew and set up control of the first completed area.

FIELD_054.context: In a narrow corridor, painters and door installers are scheduled for the same shift.
FIELD_054.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will gather the supervisors of both crews to agree passage and handover of the corridor.
options.B: I will propose a sequence of work and, together with the supervisors, confirm access and handover times.
options.C: I will propose an order of work in the corridor and, together with the supervisors, allocate access to the rooms.
options.D: I will determine a safe sequence and announce specific time windows to the sections.

FIELD_055.context: The base for tiles has a local level difference; the supervisor proposes compensating for it with a thick layer of adhesive.
FIELD_055.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will record the measurement and set an acceptable levelling method before tiling starts.
options.B: I will compare the level difference with the adhesive's limits and formalise an agreed technical solution.
options.C: I will measure the level difference and check the permissible adhesive thickness against the design and the instructions.
options.D: I will document the need to prepare the base before tiling in accordance with the approved method statement.

FIELD_056.context: The client's representative verbally proposes changing the colour of the accent wall after the material has been purchased.
FIELD_056.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will clarify the impact of the new colour on materials and personally present the conditions of the change to the client.
options.B: I will check the approved palette, the remaining stock and the impact of the change on time and cost.
options.C: I will explain directly that the change is possible after formal approval and an updated assignment.
options.D: I will present a calculation of the consequences and propose formalising the change before repainting.

FIELD_057.context: At the window reveals, two crews applied sealant differently, although both refer to the same detail.
FIELD_057.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will check the detailing, the joint width and the surface preparation requirements.
options.B: I will gather the foremen and the inspector for a joint review of the reference detail.
options.C: I will check the detail and, together with the crews, agree on a sample of correct workmanship.
options.D: I will compare the two versions of the reveal and, together with the crews, sort out the differences in understanding the detail.

FIELD_058.context: Before installing facade cassettes, the scaffold inspection log has no entry for the current shift.
FIELD_058.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will not allow anyone onto the section until the established inspection is carried out and recorded.
options.B: I will check the condition of the section with the responsible person and secure a formal permit before work.
options.C: I will request confirmation of the scaffold condition myself and enforce the established shift access procedure.
options.D: I will check that the entry is complete and the access tag is on the specific scaffold section.

FIELD_059.context: Door units were delivered to the site, and some of them lack a document confirming the required properties.
FIELD_059.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will note the incomplete set and, together with procurement, request the documents before installation.
options.B: I will agree a check of the door units with the warehouse and quality control and reflect the batch status in the register.
options.C: I will record the list of missing confirmations in the incoming inspection report.
options.D: I will contact procurement and the supplier to speed up receipt of the documents.

FIELD_060.context: One tile shade is running out earlier than calculated; another batch may differ slightly in tone.
FIELD_060.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will propose a way of distributing the tile batches and discuss its visible result with the crew.
options.B: I will make clear that I will not mix batches without an agreed layout and propose stopping work in this area.
options.C: I will gather the tilers, the warehouse and the designer to assess options for distributing the batches.
options.D: I will propose keeping the batches separate at their boundary and agree the layout together with the participants.

FIELD_061.context: During installation of facade insulation, the base temperature has approached the lower limit specified by the mix manufacturer.
FIELD_061.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will measure the base temperature at several points and check the forecast against the instructions.
options.B: I will stop using the mix while the temperature conditions remain unconfirmed and document the checks on those conditions.
options.C: I will record the measurements and schedule work only within a confirmed temperature window.
options.D: I will compare the actual temperature with the mix instructions and record the permissible work window.

FIELD_062.context: After a water test of the facade junction, a damp spot appeared on the inside with no visible leak path.
FIELD_062.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will state clearly that the joint cannot be closed without a repeat check and a decision.
options.B: I will present an observation scheme and initiate a repeat test with the responsible people.
options.C: I will compare the location of the damp spot with the junction detail and propose the next control area myself.
options.D: I will check the test report, the spray zone and possible water paths before concluding there is a defect.

FIELD_063.context: In a long corridor, laying floor tiles from both sides leads to a narrow cut at the main entrance.
FIELD_063.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will prepare two layouts based on actual dimensions and agree one on site.
options.B: I will compare two layouts at the entrance and, together with the designer, choose the basis for approval.
options.C: I will check the axes, dimensions and approved layout, then propose an option with an acceptable cut.
options.D: I will gather the designer, the supervisor and the client at the entrance to choose an acceptable axis.

FIELD_064.context: Before closing a service box, it was found that the certificate for fire-stopping the penetration has not been signed.
FIELD_064.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will personally arrange confirmation of the penetration seal and record that the box is ready to be closed.
options.B: I will note the missing fire-stopping certificate and file a request for the mandatory inspection.
options.C: I will not allow the box to be closed until the seal is checked and the certificate is issued.
options.D: I will check the penetrations against the as-built drawing and arrange an inspection before closing.

FIELD_065.context: After the rooms were painted, adjacent trades plan dusty work in the neighbouring zone without the required separation.
FIELD_065.text: Which approach would you prefer in this situation?

options.A: I will formalise a scheme for separation, cleaning and surface protection before admitting the adjacent trades.
options.B: I will contact the adjacent trades and we will discuss barriers, passages and the cleaning procedure.
options.C: I will include the protection measures in the plan and jointly check that they are ready before allowing access.
options.D: I will agree zone separation with the adjacent trades and establish the procedure for protecting painted surfaces.
